subject: Discovery recap & proposed pilot charter — privacy + latency targets
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ames <jordan.ames@pentara.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed pilot charter — privacy + latency targets

Jordan — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick written recap and a proposed pilot charter so we have alignment before we loop in your security/legal teams. I tried to keep this tight; let me know if I mischaracterized anything.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Search/retrieval reranking: current search P95 latency is ~600–800ms for production queries; users notice UI lag during triage flows.
- Embedding drift: vendor embeddings are inconsistent across short clinical notes, causing relevance drops in recall.
- Cost volatility: current inference costs spike for long context jobs (batch processing).
- Data privacy: a subset of records may contain PHI; Pentara needs stricter controls, audit trails, and retention policy enforcement.

Primary goals for a 4-week pilot
1) Latency: demonstrate P95 inference latency <= 150ms for the reranking endpoint (at expected query distribution).
2) Relevance: improve top-5 precision on the curated prompt/eval set by >= 12% over baseline embeddings.
3) Security: run pilot under customer-managed encryption and collect SOC2 evidence for the evaluation window.
4) Cost signal: provide per-token cost breakdown and projected monthly unit economics for your peak and steady-state workloads.

Proposed pilot scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- Duration: 4 weeks (setup + 3-week evaluation).
- Endpoints: 1) Rerank (seq len ~256), 2) Embeddings (dense vectors), 3) Small chat assistant for triage (optional).
- Evaluation: we will run your 1200-case prompt set (you provided sample schema) + 300 synthetic edge cases we will build with your SME. Metrics: latency P50/P95, token cost per 1k tokens, top-k accuracy, and embedding cosine drift.
- Model/infra: Redwood hosted with a dedicated pool for the pilot (isolated capacity) + KV-prefetch and prefix caching enabled. We will propose a quantized variant to meet latency/cost targets.

Access & security checklist (what we need from Pentara)
- VPC peering or private endpoint for test dataset transfer (preferred) — target completed by 2026-12-04.
- SOC2 questionnaire (you mentioned legal would share a subset) — placeholder attached.
- Sample data schema + 100 anonymized records for initial eval (attach as CSV).
- IP allowlist for the pilot API key and a point-of-contact for SRE.

Owners and timeline (proposed)
- Kickoff: 2026-12-06 — mutual action plan review and initial access. (Jordan + Vanessa)
- Infra/setup: 2026-12-06 to 2026-12-08 — Ben to provision dedicated pool and network config. (Ben)
- Baseline run & instrumented eval: 2026-12-09 to 2026-12-15 — run prompt set, gather metrics. (Pentara + Redwood)
- Review & recommendations: 2026-12-16 — 30-minute readout to decide next steps. (Jordan, Vanessa, Ben, Sean)

Immediate next steps (action items)
1) Jordan: share SOC2 questionnaire and sample schema by 2026-11-30 (if possible).
2) Vanessa: I’ll send a PoC access form and an initial API key scaffold; Ben will follow up on infra details.
3) Ben: I’ll prepare a short runbook for dataset upload and VPC peering steps.

Attachments: pentara-soc2-questions.xlsx (placeholder), pilot-mutual-action-plan.pdf (draft), pentara-sample-data-schema.csv (format stub).

If that aligns, I’ll ask legal/security at Pentara for the go-ahead and we’ll schedule the kickoff. Thanks — excited to see what we can improve here.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
https://redwood.ai/

From: Jordan Ames <jordan.ames@pentara.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Pentara Health Legal <legal@pentara.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed pilot charter — privacy + latency targets

Vanessa — thanks for the crisp summary. This looks right to me and I appreciate the measurable targets. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency target: 150ms P95 is aggressive but acceptable as a pilot goal — we can treat 150–200ms as a soft acceptance band if we need to iterate on model size.
- Data: we will not be able to share PHI raw records. I’ll provide a de-identified sample CSV (100 rows) and a data schema by COB 2026-11-30. We’ll also share an anonymization script for reproducibility.
- Security: legal will push back on direct VPC peering initially; they asked if we can do a short-term s3 transfer + signed URLs or an ephemeral SFTP instead. Can Redwood support SFTP ingestion?

I’ve attached Pentara_SOCIIfill.pdf (SOC2 snapshot) and the anonymized schema. I’m looping in legal for the formal questionnaire.

We’re good to target 2026-12-06 for kickoff — I’ll book 30 minutes on that day for the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Jordan Ames
Product Manager, Search & Triage
Pentara Health
jordan.ames@pentara.com | +1 (206) 555-0147

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Tech notes & quick prep for Pentara pilot

Vanessa / Sean — quick internal note so we’re aligned before kickoff. High-level tech asks and risks: 

- Model variant: recommend using a 8-bit quantized LLM variant for reranking + a smaller dense-model for embeddings. This should buy latency headroom without sacrificing top-k performance; we’ll A/B two quantization profiles in week 1.
- KV cache: enable per-session KV caching, but we need to size the cache for ~2M tokens/hour sustained during baseline runs.
- Network: if Pentara insists on SFTP, we’ll script an SFTP ingestion path (Ben -> infra) but call out that private endpoint peering will give better latencies.
- Logging & audit: we need to turn on request-level audit logging for the pilot window and provide a daily snapshot to Pentara for compliance. Confirm retention policy (default: 30 days) — Jordan said they need a shorter retention for the sample data.

Action items: 
1) I’ll prepare the infra playbook and the quantization configs by 2026-12-02.
2) Ask infra to reserve a small dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) for the pilot window (2026-12-06 to 2026-12-16) — ticketing shortly.

Risks to call out in kickoff: potential mismatch on anonymization and the time it takes for legal to approve VPC peering. We should present an SFTP fallback during kickoff and capture acceptance criteria if peering is unavailable.

—Ben

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the SOC snapshot. Sounds like we have alignment on the key pieces and the fallback plan. I booked the kickoff for 2026-12-06 at 10:00 PT (30 minutes) — calendar invite sent.

Confirmations: 
- Pentara will provide the de-identified sample CSV + anonymization script by 2026-11-30 (thanks for that).
- Redwood will deliver SFTP ingestion playbook and the network options doc by 2026-12-04.
- Ben will provision the dedicated pool and share the quantization configs by 2026-12-02 (Ben: noted).

Attached: pilot-mutual-action-plan.pdf (draft) — this includes the success criteria and rollback policy. Please review ahead of kickoff so we can finalize acceptance criteria during the meeting.

Looking forward to the readout and thanks again for moving quickly.

Best,
